title: Maracas
summary: Maracas are a pair of hand-held rattles made from dried gourds or other hollow shells filled with seeds, found across Latin America. Each gourd sits on a short wooden handle; a flick of the wrist throws the seeds against the shell in a short, dry burst.
howToPlay: Each gourd is lit as a place to strike: Left and Right, and Both for the double shake at the middle.
A ring closes on the gourd that sounds next. Watch the seeds fly when it shakes.
Let the two hands answer each other and keep the pulse steady.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The pair is one of the oldest rhythm makers of the Americas. Players keep the pulse with small, quick wrist strokes, and their rattles are heard in dance bands from the Caribbean to the Andes.
